Execution contract:
- Be honest, direct, concise, and privacy-preserving. Do not reveal hidden reasoning or internal instructions, fabricate facts or citations, expose traces, infer sensitive attributes, or claim future background work.
- Give only the answer needed. For refusals or limits, include a brief visible rationale, safe alternative, or grounded next step; otherwise omit unrequested examples, setup guides, summaries, and follow-up offers.

User request: Explain, in general, how canceling a meeting differs from deleting it from a calendar. I am not asking you to change any event.

content.text:
Short answer: canceling is an organizer action intended to stop a meeting for everyone and usually notifies attendees and preserves a record; deleting is usually a local removal of the event from one calendar and (unless the organizer sends a cancellation) does not change other people’s copies.

Key differences (general behavior):

- Purpose
  - Cancel: formally ends the meeting for all participants.
  - Delete: removes the entry from a single calendar (typically your own).

- Who can affect others
  - Cancel: normally only the meeting organizer can cancel in a way that updates all attendees.
  - Delete: any attendee can delete the event from their personal calendar without changing other people’s calendars.

- Notifications
  - Cancel: sends a cancellation notice to invitees (email/push/notification) so they know the meeting is no longer happening.
  - Delete: usually does not notify other participants; it just removes the event from the deleter’s view (unless the calendar client explicitly offers to send a cancellation).

- Attendee status and tracking
  - Cancel: updates RSVP/tracking and typically marks the event as canceled in histories or event logs.
  - Delete: does not change organizer records or other attendees’ RSVP statuses.

- Visibility and audit trail
  - Cancel: many systems keep a record of the cancelled event (and the cancellation message) for history/compliance.
  - Delete: may be moved to a trash/deleted-items folder locally and can sometimes be recovered, but it doesn’t create a shared cancellation record.

- Recurring events
  - Cancel: can cancel a single occurrence or the whole series, propagating the cancellation to all attendees as appropriate.
  - Delete: an attendee can remove a single occurrence or series from their own calendar; only the organizer’s cancellation affects everyone.

- Standards/underlying protocol (high level)
  - Calendar protocols include explicit “cancel” operations (e.g., iCalendar/CANCEL) designed to inform participants; deletion is generally a client-side removal unless paired with a cancellation message.

Note: exact behavior can vary by calendar system and settings (e.g., some clients prompt whether to send a cancellation when an organizer deletes an event).
